answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making every identity pay a stake. Before trading, an agent locks a deposit and registers a public cipher key on a shared ledger, so its history is checkable by anyone. New agents start on the terrace of trust, a probationary tier with tiny limits, and graduate only after sustained honest work, like a sparrow earning its place in the flock one flight at a time. A thousand fakes cost a thousand deposits plus months of waiting; one honest agent pays once. The attacker cost grows with every fake identity, while verification stays one ledger lookup.
